key_insight: Adapting both model choice and stopping to observed outputs and congestion minimizes long-run classification costs, while fixed-order cascades can be arbitrarily more costly under the same query-depth limit.
engineering_relevance: Shared LLM classification services can balance error penalties, query fees, and latency costs by pricing the congestion each additional query creates.
method: Represent adaptive routing policies as mixtures of decision trees and formulate a convex optimization problem.
Use marginal congestion prices in a Bayesian dynamic program to choose models and stopping decisions.
Compute policies with column generation and an explicit optimality-gap bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments separating the benefits of adaptive model selection and congestion-aware design, but provides no datasets or quantitative results.
watch_item: Exact holding-cost results rely on specified queueing assumptions: exponential service times for first-come-first-served servers or general service times under processor sharing.
paper_title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
